what: The friends default for games with no character, built and gated (stream friends-default).

creator.words: You can fix seeing your friend default.
creator.context: The bar since 2026-10-05 is "friends are in one game, in sync, and each player sees the others as a character"; what that means for a board, card or puzzle game was the open question in DESIGN ("Still open") and in the PA11 eval case's interim reading.

decision.rule: How a friend is seen is the game's shape, chosen from how friends play together and whether a player is a character, never per game (gf/mp/presence.js shapeOf).

shapes.character: the players walk the world: each sees the others where they really are (unchanged)
shapes.seats: nobody is a character, one shared board or table: a seat card per friend (name, colour, an avatar that reacts: waiting, thinking on their turn, placed just after a move, won, lost, away), their pointer moving where they point, and a ring in their colour where each of their moves lands, on every screen
shapes.boards: nobody is a character, each player has their own board: each friend's board drawn live beside yours, framed in their colour, with their name, score, avatar, pointer and last move

decision.chosen_by: a part's manifest says when it holds every player's body (holds: the board played from the seats is a mark, a board of one's own is a board); a game whose own code holds the players says multiplayer.presence; create writes config/game.json players.presence; the loop holds a spec to the ledger's body line and stops asking what a friend looks like when the shape answers it
decision.prior_art: the Brickbloom live-boards pilot (games.fun research/foundations/evidence/multiplayer-live-boards-pilot-2026-10-06.json, commit 81ec523b8), never judged by the creator; PA11's interim reading ("a named marker where they are about to play") and its two builds, which made the players characters walking a giant board

gate.how: the presence leg (builder/tools/lib/presence-check.mjs): two players over real WebRTC; what the game must show comes from its locked spec and parts, never its config; each screen must show the other in that shape; each player makes moves with the real mouse where their screen lists them, and each must land on the other screen within 3 s, with their pointer

regressions.board-friend-unseen: mustFail E · 5 (Table Four with its settings saying the players are characters)
regressions.own-board-unseen: mustFail E · 5 (Lights Race shown as seats)

runs.table-four: verify, every build measure: PASS gates 6/6, measures 22/22 in 183 s; presence leg 2 of 2 moves each way within 3 s, both pointers seen
runs.lights-race: first verify FAIL A (look.time dusk not a jelly-pastel option) and D 12 (score only +1 at the end: nothing built up in a timed round); fixed in the example (day; the score is the lights switched off, from each move); then PASS gates 6/6, measures 22/22 in 185 s; presence leg 2 of 2 each way
runs.giant-four: verify after the board changes (shape character, no presence part): PASS gates 6/6, measures 22/22 in 169 s
runs.regressions_first_run: board-friend-unseen ok, own-board-unseen ok; lights-race-friends-seen failed kit-identical because this session rewrote gf-multiplayer's SHA256SUMS while the run was going (the presence leg itself passed); table-four-friends-seen failed the gate's background-host step once under load (an npm test and a forge verify on the machine) and passed it alone right after (verify --check 5, 97 s)
runs.screenshots: 2026-10-14-friends-default/: each player's own screen right after the first moves (Table Four and Lights Race, host and joiner)

forge_gate_flag.asked: remove the forge ?gf-gate=1 check.query if the live gate holds without it
forge_gate_flag.run: ruin-hold, multiplayer.json without check.query, verify --check 5: PASS, but only because forge's measure 5 lets a soft check pass: the gate's own record says round 1 ended before the background-host step and round 2 was not running either, so that step was never checked
forge_gate_flag.kept: the flag stays (create still writes it): without it forge loses the background-host proof. It also serves the loadout leg and forge's pickup walk.

not_done: Nobody has played it; the creator has not seen it.
Two Chrome contexts on one machine; no real network, no phone, not at 4K.
Seats and boards are drawn by the three runtime only (forge, vista and godot games all have characters today).
The avatar is one stand-in face (ui.avatar) on a disc of the player's colour, not a portrait of the player's own body.
Four players were not run; the boards column is sized for three friends.
Bodies at the board stand where the board's seats put them: on the plaza one stands in the fountain (the board clears props, not the fountain).
